about.title: About Emergency Fund Calculator
about.description: The Emergency Fund Calculator helps you estimate how much money to set aside for unexpected expenses and financial disruptions. It calculates a suggested emergency fund range based on monthly expenses, income stability, and personal risk factors. Use it as a planning reference when reviewing savings targets for job loss, medical expenses, or other unplanned costs.

faq.q: How much should I have in my emergency fund?
faq.a: Most financial experts recommend 3-6 months of essential expenses. If you have stable employment, 3 months may suffice. If you're self-employed, have variable income, or work in an unstable industry, aim for 6-9 months of expenses.

faq.q: Where should I keep my emergency fund?
faq.a: Keep your emergency fund in easily accessible accounts like high-yield savings accounts, money market accounts, or short-term CDs. Avoid investing emergency funds in stocks or other volatile investments that could lose value when you need the money.

faq.q: Should I pay off debt or build an emergency fund first?
faq.a: Start with a small emergency fund ($500-1,000), then focus on high-interest debt. Once high-interest debt is paid off, build your full 3-6 month emergency fund. This prevents you from going further into debt during emergencies.

faq.q: What counts as an emergency expense?
faq.a: True emergencies include job loss, major medical expenses, urgent home or car repairs, and unexpected family emergencies. Vacations, holidays, or planned purchases are not emergencies and should be budgeted separately.
